1.w: Like snow in summer or rain in harvest, so honor is not fitting for a fool.

2.w: Like a fluttering bird or like a flying swallow, so a curse without cause does not come to rest.

3.w: A whip for the horse and a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the backs of fools!

4.w: Do not answer a fool according to his folly, lest you yourself also be like him.

5.w: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own opinion.

6.w: Like cutting off the feet or drinking violence, so is sending a message by the hand of a fool.

7.w: Like legs dangle uselessly from the lame, so a proverb dangles in the mouth of fools.

8.w: Like tying a stone in a sling, so is giving honor to a fool.

9.w: Like a thorn has gone up into the hand of a drunkard, so a proverb has gone up into the mouth of a fool.

10.w: Like an archer who wounds at random, so is the one who hires a fool or hires any passerby.

11.w: Like a dog that returns to its vomit, so a fool repeats his folly.

12.w: You have seen a man wise in his own opinion — there is more hope for a fool than for him.

13.w: The sluggard has said, “There is a lion in the road! A lion in the streets!”

14.w: Like a door that turns on its hinges, so a sluggard turns on his bed.

15.w: The sluggard has plunged his hand in the dish; he is too lazy to bring it back to his mouth.

16.w: The sluggard is wiser in his own opinion than seven people who respond with good sense.

17.w: Like one who grabs a wild dog by the ears, so is the person passing by who becomes furious over a quarrel not his own.

18.w: Like a madman who shoots firebrands and deadly arrows,

19.w: so is a person who has deceived his neighbor, and said, “Was I not only joking?”

20.w: Where there is no wood, a fire goes out, and where there is no gossip, contention ceases.

21.w: Like charcoal is to burning coals, and wood to fire, so is a contentious person to kindle strife.

22.w: The words of a gossip are like choice morsels; and they have gone down into a person’s innermost being.

23.w: Like a coating of glaze over earthenware are fervent lips with an evil heart.

24.w: The one who hates others disguises it with his lips, but he stores up deceit within him.

25.w: When he speaks graciously, do not believe him, for there are seven abominations within him.

26.w: Though his hatred may be concealed by deceit, his evil will be uncovered in the assembly.

27.w: The one who digs a pit will fall into it; the one who rolls a stone—it will come back on him.

28.w: A lying tongue hates those crushed by it, and a flattering mouth works ruin.
